newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-firm - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-firm - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Wednesday were seen steady to firm amid outlooks for continued tight hog marketings, livestock dealers said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hog receipts Tuesday were estimated at 95,000 head versus 89,000 a week ago and 100,000 a year ago.

Cash hog prices also could be underpinned by ongoing strength in fresh loin prices, which fueled packer demand Tuesday, sources said. Some of the strength also was tied to possible export demand, although confirmation was elusive, several sources said.

"Packers could be buying hogs to meet expected (pork) export demand," said Dale Benson, livestock analyst with Dean-Witter Reynolds in Chicago. He said Japanese pork import price restrictions were seen lifted by the end of June, and some packers could be stocking up on loins in anticipation of Japanese business.

Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to plants were seen ranging from $61.00 to $61.50 per cwt and Illinois top prices at plants could span $60.00 to $60.50, sources in those areas said. Indiana/Ohio top prices at the plant could range $60.50 to $61.00, dealers there said.
